A tactical starfighter dogfighting game for 2 players, 45 minutes, with big detailed minis and four very different factions to fly. Every pilot plans a maneuver in secret, then everyone moves at once. Guess right, and you're on their tail. Guess wrong, and they're on yours.

What is Star Squadron? Two pilots. A hex field. Forty-five minutes.

Each round you secretly choose a maneuver card, then both sides reveal and move simultaneously. No waiting for your turn, no take-backs. The whole game lives in that moment of "where do I think they're going?"

Four factions. One hex field. No turns.

Every round in Star Squadron you pick a maneuver behind your screen, then both sides reveal and move at the same time. Big starfighter minis on a hex battle board, 2 players, 45 minutes.

FACTION SPOTLIGHT: The Eisenkiesel Empire

A galaxy-spanning military empire that fights the way Earth would: complex electronic weapons housed in solid metal. When diplomacy fails, they send in the fighters. And lately, diplomacy has been failing a lot.

Eisenkiesel pilots fly through neuro-interfaces, reacting nearly as fast as thought, and they are fiercely competitive, out-doing even their own squadmates to earn promotion. Their science is methodical and no-nonsense, with no room for spirituality. They deny there is anything living inside the energy crystals at all.

On the table: Target-Lock Missiles (lead your target for two turns, then fire for big damage at zero energy) and Afterburner tokens for a burst of speed after moves are revealed. The most down-to-earth faction to fly, and the designer's personal favorite.

Which faction would you fly? Tell us below. 👇

The maneuver board is the heart of Star Squadron.

Every pilot picks a move, face-down, at the same time. Banks, slides, loops, splits, and each pilot's own special move. Then everyone flips and the ships move together. There's no hiding behind turn order, just reading your opponent.

FACTION SPOTLIGHT: The Vermarine Hive

An ecosystem spanning many star systems, where every organism has a role it was bio-engineered to fill. Nothing in the Hive is manufactured. It is grown, including the starfighters, which are closer to war beasts than machines.

A Vermarine pilot forms a life-long bond with their ship through pheromones and more, and in a dogfight the two act as one, like horse and rider. Their ships survive the void by ingesting energy crystals. One crystal lasts years, but there are rumors the ships are growing more ravenous, and more savage in the hunt.

On the table: pilot abilities that reroll dice (yours or your opponent's), Ion Cannons that drain an enemy's boost or weapon energy instead of shields, and Repair Drones you have to decide when to spend. Too early and you waste them. Too late and you're already dust.

FACTION SPOTLIGHT: The Order of Citrine

A galaxy-spanning religious order with one purpose: gather the shattered fragments of the holy realm that fell into our space. Those fragments are the energy crystals, and any other use of them is sacrilege. All crystals belong to the Order by birthright, and they will collect them at blaster-point if they have to.

Citrine pilots commune with their crystals in sacred chambers, bathing in golden light that burns and scars them, singing hymns the whole time. They come away with visions: futures to fight for, and futures to fight against. Whatever is inside those crystals hears them. Starved of the chorus of Hyperspace, it grows to believe it is an angel. Or a god. The crystal turns gold.

On the table: prophecy dice you pre-roll before the round and substitute in later, shields you can angle to the front or rear, and an auxiliary battery for an instant energy recharge. Defensive until they strike, and when they strike it's decisive.

Every Citrine pilot's surname is a legendary sword. Name them in the comments.

FACTION SPOTLIGHT: The Amethyst Warlords

Nobody knows where the necro-tech black goo came from. A mass of self-replicating, semi-aware nanomachines, and whatever it was meant for, it is now the ultimate tool for gaining power. A Warlord lets the goo wash over their body and emerges a cybernetic, near-immortal lich. Then they build ships from it, with an energy crystal at the heart of each one, and go hunting for thralls.

The only thing stopping the Warlords from conquering the galaxy is each other. Any thrall who keeps their will during the process turns on their master and starts a warband of their own. They believe the crystals hold the ghosts of a long-dead civilization, and that pain releases power. The crystals turn a sickly violet.

On the table: positional pilot abilities that reward formation flying, energy mines dropped behind your ship that force your opponent into predictable moves, and torpedoes whose damage depends on how the target maneuvers. Positional advantage, or just big damage.

That's all four. Which one is yours?

Build your loadout.

Pick a ship class: Interceptor (fast, light), Superiority Fighter (tight turns, built to kill fighters), or Fighter-Bomber (heaviest armor, steady advance). Slot a special weapon: Laser Cannon for hitscan damage, Homing Plasma that can't miss, or the Spread Vulcan that shreds everything in your front arc. Then choose a pilot with their own special maneuver. Ship stats decide how many dice you roll. Pilot skill decides what you need to roll.

No two squadrons play alike, and the rulebook has symmetrical, asymmetrical, draft, power-up, and point-buy modes for building them.

5 days left. Back it on Kickstarter, link in bio.

What's in the box.

A Battle Box is a complete game: two full squadrons of big starfighter minis on flight stands, ship cards, pilot cards, special weapon cards, double-sided battle boards with hex terrain, maneuver boards, player screens, energy trackers, tokens, and dice. Four objective types, modular terrain variants, and a campaign mode are all in the rulebook.

Box 1 is Eisenkiesel vs Vermarine. Box 2 is Citrine vs Amethyst. One box is head-to-head. Two boxes is 4-player free-for-all or 2v2.

4 days left. Back it on Kickstarter, link in bio.

Star Squadron is packed with Easter eggs for sci-fi fans.

The Eisenkiesel ships: FS-22 Velociraptor, FS-35 Thunderbolt III, FS-16 Peregrine. Can you name the real-world fighters they reference?

The Eisenkiesel pilots are mash-ups of pop-culture aces: Hoban Rook, Alex Danvers, Rei Takagi, James Colasour. Vermarine pilots are Latin flower-mammal combos. Citrine pilots are named for legendary swords.

Drop your decodes in the comments. 3 days left on Kickstarter. Back it on Kickstarter, link in bio.

48 hours.

Why are they fighting? Scattered across the galaxy, motes of pure energy coalesce over millennia into crystals. Energy quartz. Star quartz. Whatever you call them, they power thrusters, shields, and directed-energy weapons, and at the heart of each one is a singularity that opens into Hyperspace. First contact happened because of them. Then the skirmishes started. Then the war.

And something is accelerating it.
